A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PLEIADES. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching despite rewriting and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original gesture-recognition, eye-tracking and roadscene-detection results, plus temporal-resampling, masking and quantization-sparsity analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds polynomial-degree and Jacobi-parameter sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.1.2.

M1.justification: The polynomial kernel expansion, discretization, contraction optimization, causal backbone and task heads remain substantively unchanged, including the default degree four and Jacobi parameters (-0.25, -0.25). Parameter sweeps and prospective recurrent/spiking extensions do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use DVS128 gestures, AIS2024 eye tracking and Prophesee GEN4 detection. Naming the eye-tracking dataset 3ET+ clarifies existing coverage. The new 200 ms sensitivity experiments remain within the gesture task and latency conditions already examined.

E2.justification: GEN4 Table 3 adds S5-ViT-B and GET-T alongside the retained RED and Gray-RetinaNet baselines. Comparator membership in the gesture-recognition and eye-tracking benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds MACs/sec comparisons and controlled sensitivity protocols fixing latency at 200 ms while varying degree or Jacobi parameters. Retained benchmark preprocessing, binning, masking and resampling procedures are unchanged; newly documented training budgets do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1.2 adds focused sensitivity studies comparing degrees 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10 with free kernels, and nine Jacobi-parameter pairs. These refine the existing structured-versus-free comparison; masking, resampling and quantization-sparsity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts. v4 states 25 trials except for GEN4 and reports means with standard errors in Tables 1–2 and 6–7, with a normal-noise assumption. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase over v1's unspecified run count.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and Figure 3 curves are retained. Added results include operation counts, S5-ViT-B's 0.478 and GET-T's 0.484 mAP, and sensitivity results such as 73.2% for degree four versus 52.3% for free kernels at 200 ms. Section 5.1 changes warm-up latency from 440 to 450 ms, while Table 1 retains 0.44 seconds.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit memory-scaling argument from O(kHW) buffering to O(nHW) recurrent basis projections. The polynomial expansion, discretization derivation and Appendix A contraction-cost analysis otherwise remain substantively the same; no new proof establishes the proposed recurrent alternative.

C1.justification: The central claims remain polynomial temporal kernels for efficient causal event processing, resampling without fine-tuning, and state-of-the-art performance on three benchmarks. The abstract retains the same headline results; added supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1.2 newly interprets excessive degree as overfitting temporal noise and describes Jacobi-parameter effects as borderline significant. Section 6 presents the recurrent memory workaround more definitively than v1's approximation discussion, while retaining the buffering limitation. The conclusion also revises the proposed spiking-conversion rationale.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies training epochs, batch sizes, A30 walltimes and VRAM usage; dataset access and licensing notes are also added. Conversely, v1's code and pretrained-model access statement disappears. This establishes removal of access information, not that the resources themselves became unavailable.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on STREAM, S7, optimal SSM tensor contractions and newer detection methods, and explicitly positions PLEIADES as generalizing SLAYER's response kernels. The Lebesgue-sampling and Huh–Sejnowski references disappear. The broader LMU/HiPPO/state-space positioning remains.

P1.justification: Substantial prose rewriting spans the introduction, related work, method explanations, experiments, limitations and conclusion. v4 removes the introductory roadmap, reorganizes explanations into clearer enumerations, changes citation style and terminology, and adds PLEIADES to the title. This exceeds localized copyediting.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain their artwork, with Figure 3 relocated. Tables 1 and 3 gain computational-cost/frame-rate columns, benchmark rows are reordered, and two sensitivity tables are added. The earlier architecture table is retained as Table 8; these are localized display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's point estimates and fixed polynomial choices, v4 adds uncertainty reporting, controlled sensitivity studies, newer comparison baselines and concrete training/compute details. These improve evidential support and transparency, partly offset by removal of the code/model access statement and conflicting 450 ms versus 0.44-second warm-up values.
